definition: In machine learning, first-order inductive learner (FOIL) is a rule-based learning algorithm.
details: In machine learning, first-order inductive learner (FOIL) is a rule-based learning algorithm.

explainer.lead: FOIL is a machine-learning algorithm that learns if–then rules from examples. Its results can be read as statements about relationships, making it useful when people need to inspect what the learner has found.

tiers.eli5: It learns by building a set of if-then rules from examples, adding one condition at a time until the rule covers the right cases and few wrong ones.
tiers.practitioner: Each rule starts from a general clause and is specialised greedily by adding literals that improve coverage of positives without pulling in negatives; the classic pitfall is overfitting from noisy data and the combinatorial cost of searching literal combinations.
tiers.paperLevel: Rules are learned in first-order logic: each clause is grown by adding literals that maximise a gain measure over covered positive and negative examples, then covered positives are removed and the process repeats; greedy search gives no optimality guarantee and scaling is limited.

explainer.example: Given parent(Ann,Bob), parent(Bob,Cid), and other family examples, FOIL could learn grandparent(X,Z) :- parent(X,Y), parent(Y,Z). Because Ann is Bob's parent and Bob is Cid's parent, the rule concludes that Ann is Cid's grandparent.
explainer.goal: Learn readable rules that capture patterns in relational examples and can be applied to new cases.
inputs: Properties and relationships expressed in first-order form
outputs: A set of learned if–then rules
Conclusions produced by applying those rules
steps: Provide examples and their known relationships
Construct candidate rules from those relationships
Retain rules that explain the examples
Apply the learned rules to new cases
tradeoffs: Learned rules are relatively easy for people to read
First-order rules can express relationships between entities
Searching possible rules can become expensive
Results depend on how examples and relationships are represented

diagram.caption: FOIL uses examples to select rules, then applies those rules to new cases.
